prompt.context_jp: 甘春総合病院の廊下に、慌ただしい足音___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春総合病院の廊下に、慌ただしい足音___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Opening scene-setting line. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is the first line of the chapter and the footsteps are brand-new information being introduced into the scene. が marks this neutral-description/new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 足音 as an already-established topic, which doesn't fit an opening description. を would mark an object, but 響く is intransitive here.

contrast_examples.en: Footsteps rang out in the hallway. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: その足音は五十嵐のものだった。
contrast_examples.en: Those footsteps were Igarashi's. (already known topic)

prompt.context_jp: オレンジと黒、一対の風船___天井近くで揺れている。
prompt.prompt_jp: オレンジと黒、一対の風船___天井近くで揺れている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this descriptive sentence?

feedback.correct_en: The balloons are freshly introduced into the hallway scene — a neutral description of what exists there. が marks this new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 風船 was already the topic under discussion. に marks a location/direction, not the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: その風船は子供たちのプレゼントだ。
contrast_examples.en: Those balloons are the kids' gift. (topic already known)

prompt.context_jp: 点滴が入り、久美の呼吸___ようやく落ち着きを取り戻した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 点滴が入り、久美の呼吸___ようやく落ち着きを取り戻した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits here?

feedback.correct_en: Kumi is already the established focus of the scene; the narrator takes '久美の呼吸' as the topic and comments on how it finally settled. は marks that topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the breathing as fresh new information, but we've been watching Kumi the whole scene. を is wrong — 取り戻す here is about what the breathing did, not what acts on it.

contrast_examples.jp: 呼吸はようやく落ち着いた。

contrast_examples.en: Suddenly her breathing became erratic. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 母親の絞り出すような独白を耳にして、彼___そのまま黙って立ち去ることができなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___そのまま黙って立ち去ることができなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Igarashi here?

feedback.correct_en: The paragraph is continuing to describe Igarashi — he's the established topic. は keeps him as the theme while the sentence comments on what he couldn't do.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce 彼 as new information, which clashes with the fact he was just named in the previous sentence.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は立ち去れなかった。

prompt.context_jp: どうして久美ちゃんがハロウィンをやろうと思ったのか、それ___お友達のためだったんです。
prompt.prompt_jp: それ___お友達のためだったんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi explains Kumi's reason. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 'それ' refers back to the just-mentioned reason — it's the topic being commented on. は signals 'as for that, it was for her friend.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single out それ as the exhaustive answer in a direct identificational focus, which feels too clipped for this gentle explanation. を is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.jp: それは友達のためでした。
contrast_examples.en: That was for her friend. (topic → comment)

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐の声___沈黙のなかに落ちていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐の声___沈黙のなかに落ちていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrative descriptive line. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: This is a cinematic, neutral description of an event in the scene — his voice falling into silence. が is the natural choice for this kind of presentational narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would set 五十嵐の声 up as a topic for extended comment, but the sentence is a one-shot image. で doesn't fit this grammar at all.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の声はいつも穏やかだ。
contrast_examples.en: His voice is always gentle. (general topic)

prompt.context_jp: 杏___その小さな家族の光景から目を離せなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 杏___その小さな家族の光景から目を離せなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks An here?

feedback.correct_en: An has been the focus of this examination-room passage. The narrator keeps her as the topic and comments on her emotional reaction. は fits topic-continuation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present An as newly on stage, but the scene has been following her. を already appears in '目を離せなかった'.

contrast_examples.jp: 杏は目を離せなかった。
そこへ杏が入ってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 若い夫婦の、幸せそうな一対の笑顔___そこに写っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 若い夫婦の、幸せそうな一対の笑顔___そこに写っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Describing what's in the photo. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The smiling couple is being newly revealed as the content of the photo — a classic 'there was X in the picture' description. が marks this presentational subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would need 笑顔 to be an established topic, which it isn't — this is the first mention. に doesn't fit the grammatical slot of the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 写真に二人の笑顔が写っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Two smiling faces appeared in the photo. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: その笑顔は彼女のものだ。

prompt.context_jp: (大森渚について)彼女___書類を丁寧に閉じ、微笑を保ったまま話を切り出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___書類を丁寧に閉じ、微笑を保ったまま話を切り出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 彼女 here?

feedback.correct_en: The previous sentence just introduced 大森渚 by name, and this sentence continues to describe her actions. は keeps her as the established topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as new, but she was just named. を doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女はゆっくり話し始めた。
contrast_examples.en: She slowly began to speak. (topic continuation)

contrast_examples.jp: そこへ彼女が入ってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 小野寺は五十嵐を技師として守ろうとしている。「その一線だけ___、譲るつもりがなかった。」
prompt.prompt_jp: その一線だけ___、譲るつもりがなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 「だけ」 here?

feedback.correct_en: '~だけは' sets this one specific line apart from everything else — a contrastive は: 'this line in particular, he wouldn't yield on.' It emphasizes exclusion.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would single it out as the exhaustive subject of 譲るつもりがなかった, which doesn't match the contrastive 'at least this much' feel. を is wrong grammatically with this structure.

contrast_examples.en: This one thing, at least, I can't give up. (contrastive)
Only this is the problem. (exhaustive subject)

prompt.context_jp: 技師長___仲間を見守るとき、いつも中庸を心得た距離を取る男である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 技師長___仲間を見守るとき、いつも中庸を心得た距離を取る男である。
prompt.prompt_en: A general-characterization sentence about Onodera. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic characterization ('the chief tech is the kind of man who...'). Generic/habitual statements take は on the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into a specific identification ('it is the chief tech who...'), which doesn't fit this descriptive portrait. に is wrong for this slot.

contrast_examples.en: My father is a kind person. (generic description)
The kind one is my father. (exclusive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 陽子が最後の一言を絞り出すと、部屋の空気___止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の空気___止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: After Yoko's confession, how does the narration describe what happened?

feedback.correct_en: The air of the room 'freezing' is a sudden, vivid event newly observed at that moment. が marks this new-information/presentational subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 部屋の空気 an ongoing topic, but the point is the instantaneous change. を is wrong — 止まる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: For a moment, the air froze. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: この部屋の空気はいつも重い。
contrast_examples.en: The air in this room is always heavy. (general topic)

prompt.context_jp: 陽子の頬を、堪えきれなくなった涙___ひとすじ流れ落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 陽子の頬を、堪えきれなくなった涙___ひとすじ流れ落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 涙 here?

feedback.correct_en: A single tear appearing is a fresh, vivid event in the narration — presentational new information. が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 涙 as a long-standing topic, which clashes with the sudden single-tear image. に is for location/direction.

contrast_examples.jp: 涙は見せたくなかった。
contrast_examples.en: As for tears, she didn't want to show them. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 言葉を選ぶことに気をつけながら、彼はそっと病室の扉___叩いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼はそっと病室の扉___叩いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 叩く here?

feedback.correct_en: 叩く is a transitive verb taking a direct object. The door is the thing being knocked, so を is correct.
feedback.incorrect_en: 扉に叩いた doesn't work for 'knock on the door' in this construction; で would mark means ('using the door'), which is nonsensical here.

contrast_examples.en: (awkward — ノックする typically takes を too)

prompt.context_jp: 数日後、院内の会議室___、小野寺は思いがけない相手と向き合っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 院内の会議室___、小野寺は思いがけない相手と向き合っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the meeting location?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action takes place. The meeting/facing happens in the conference room.
feedback.incorrect_en: に marks existence or destination, not the setting of an active event like 向き合う. を marks a direct object.

contrast_examples.en: We discussed it in the conference room. (action location)
He was in the conference room. (existence)

prompt.context_jp: 母の魚谷雅子は放心したように椅子に沈み、甘春杏___自らを責めるような目で娘の寝顔を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春杏___自らを責めるような目で娘の寝顔を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle contrasts An with the mother in the previous clause?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts two people: the mother sinks into her chair, while An stares at the girl with self-blaming eyes. は on each subject sets up this parallel contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark An as new neutral info, losing the explicit contrast with 雅子は. も ('also') wouldn't fit because the two reactions are different, not parallel.

contrast_examples.jp: 母は泣き、杏は黙っていた。
contrast_examples.en: The mother cried; An stayed silent. (contrastive は)

contrast_examples.jp: そこへ杏が入ってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 入院着の男の子が、久美___向かって菓子袋を差し出している姿だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 久美___向かって菓子袋を差し出している姿だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle pairs with 向かって here?

feedback.correct_en: 〜に向かって is a fixed pattern meaning 'facing/toward ~'. The target of the facing takes に.
feedback.incorrect_en: を向かって is ungrammatical; で would mark means or location, not the direction being faced.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に向かって手を振った。

prompt.context_jp: 点滴が入り、久美の呼吸はようやく___を取り戻した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 久美の呼吸はようやく___を取り戻した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun collocates with 呼吸 + 取り戻す here?

feedback.correct_en: 呼吸が落ち着きを取り戻す — 'breathing regains its calmness' — is the natural pairing for a patient settling down after distress.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気を取り戻す fits a person recovering overall energy, not breathing specifically. 意識を取り戻す means 'regain consciousness' — that would apply to Kumi herself, not her breathing.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちが落ち着きを取り戻した。
患者が意識を取り戻した。

prompt.context_jp: 検査ひとつにこれほど怯えさせてしまったのかという悔いが、細い肩に重く___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 悔いが、細い肩に重く___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'regret weighing heavily on her shoulders'?

feedback.correct_en: のしかかる is the standard metaphorical verb for an emotional burden pressing down on someone's shoulders.
feedback.incorrect_en: かかわる means 'to be involved with' — no weight metaphor. ぶつかる means 'to collide,' which doesn't fit the image of a slow, heavy weight.

contrast_examples.jp: 責任が肩にのしかかる。

prompt.context_jp: 雅子の目に、ゆっくりと涙が___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 雅子の目に、ゆっくりと涙が___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb describes tears welling up slowly?

feedback.correct_en: 涙が滲む describes tears quietly welling up in the eyes — the delicate, gradual moment the author wants here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流れる means tears already running down. 降る is for rain/snow; it isn't used for tears forming in eyes.

contrast_examples.en: Tears welled up in her eyes.

prompt.context_jp: たまきの言葉は、まるで医師の説明を先取りするかのように穏やかで、しかし___に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし___に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun fits 'full of ___' here?

feedback.correct_en: 確信に満ちる ('filled with conviction') is the standard phrase. Tamaki speaks gently but with full certainty.
feedback.incorrect_en: 確認 ('confirmation/checking') and 確率 ('probability') are nouns but don't collocate with 〜に満ちる in this emotional sense.

prompt.context_jp: 陽子が最後の一言を___と、部屋の空気が止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 陽子が最後の一言を___と、部屋の空気が止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb describes forcing out difficult words?

feedback.correct_en: 言葉を絞り出す means to painfully squeeze out words you can barely say — exactly the emotional confession Yoko is making.
feedback.incorrect_en: 吐き出す is 'to spit out' and sounds angry or venting, not anguished. 差し出す is 'to hold out/offer' (physical objects), not words.

contrast_examples.jp: やっと言葉を絞り出した。
contrast_examples.en: She finally squeezed the words out.

prompt.context_jp: 祐一は一度、大きく息を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 祐一は一度、大きく息を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'taking a deep breath'?

feedback.correct_en: 息を吸い込む is to breathe in deeply — the preparation for saying something important, which fits Yuichi gathering his resolve.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を吐き出す means to breathe out (sigh). 持ち出す means 'to take out/bring up' and doesn't collocate with 息 naturally.

contrast_examples.en: He took a deep breath in.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女は書類を丁寧に閉じ、微笑を___まま話を切り出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 微笑を___まま話を切り出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'while keeping a smile'?

feedback.correct_en: 微笑を保つ ('maintain a smile') is the standard collocation for keeping a composed expression during a serious conversation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 守る means 'protect/defend' — doesn't collocate with facial expressions. 持つ ('hold/have') is too literal and unnatural with 微笑.

prompt.context_jp: 母親 Masako's reaction when Igarashi starts explaining about Kumi.
prompt.prompt_jp: Which phrasing sounds more natural for describing Masako's reaction?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the more natural line.

choices.text: 雅子は驚いた顔を上げ、それでも小さくうなずいた。
雅子は驚いた顔を立て、それでも小さくうなずいた。

feedback.correct_en: 顔を上げる ('raise one's face / look up') is the standard phrase for lifting one's gaze. It fits the narrative of her looking up at Igarashi.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔を立てる means something entirely different — it's a set idiom meaning 'to save someone's face/honor,' not physically lifting a face.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi knocks at Masako's hospital room door and asks for a moment to talk.
prompt.prompt_jp: Which opening sounds more natural and appropriate for this situation?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the more natural line.

choices.text: 失礼します。あの… 少しよろしいでしょうか。
失礼します。あの… 少しいいですか。

feedback.correct_en: In a hospital, speaking to a patient's family you don't know well, よろしいでしょうか is the appropriately polite and considerate form — matching Igarashi's careful, hesitant approach.
feedback.incorrect_en: いいですか is grammatical but noticeably more casual; it would sound a bit too familiar for a technician addressing a grieving mother he barely knows.

contrast_examples.jp: 少しお時間よろしいでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: May I have a moment of your time? (polite)

prompt.context_jp: Yuichi, emotional, begs his wife Yoko to have the surgery.
prompt.prompt_jp: Which line fits Yuichi's register as a young husband pleading with his wife?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the more natural line in context.

choices.text: 金のことなら絶対俺が何とかするから！ だから安心して手術受けてください。お願いします。
金のことなら絶対私が何とかいたしますので、ご安心の上、手術をお受けくださいませ。

feedback.correct_en: Yuichi is a young husband speaking emotionally to his wife. 俺 + casual plain speech shifting to ください/お願いします matches his heartfelt, slightly rough register perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: The overly formal keigo in b (私/いたします/くださいませ) sounds like a department-store clerk, which is bizarre between a married couple in a private moment.

contrast_examples.jp: 俺が何とかするから、安心して。
contrast_examples.en: I'll handle it, so don't worry. (intimate/casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 私が何とかいたします。
contrast_examples.en: I will take care of it. (formal business)

prompt.context_jp: Chief tech Onodera is commenting casually to a subordinate about Igarashi.
prompt.prompt_jp: Which phrasing matches Onodera's gruff-but-affectionate register?
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the more natural line.

choices.text: あいつ時々空気読めないことやるけどよ、だけどホントは誰よりも人の心が見えるのかもな。
あの方は時々空気を読めない行動をされますが、本当は誰よりも人の心がお見えになるのかもしれませんね。

feedback.correct_en: Onodera is the chief tech speaking informally to his team. あいつ, 〜けどよ, 〜のかもな carry his rough, warm senior-coworker register — exactly the version from the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: b uses honorific 敬語 (お見えになる, ご行動) toward Igarashi, which is impossible when Onodera is Igarashi's superior speaking about him to a colleague.

contrast_examples.jp: あの方はご立派な方です。
contrast_examples.en: He is a distinguished person. (overly formal here)
